claims.text: In a sync, Argo CD orders the resources it applies by phase, then by sync wave (lower first), then by kind, then by name; the file a manifest came from does not set the order.
claims.source_hint: Argo CD docs: User Guide > Sync Phases and Waves (How do I configure waves / how does it work: ordering by phase, wave, kind, name)

claims.text: An annotation is a key/value under metadata.annotations that, unlike a label, is not used to select objects. The sync wave is set with the annotation argocd.argoproj.io/sync-wave (string value, e.g. "1"); a resource without it is in wave 0.
claims.source_hint: Kubernetes docs: Concepts > Overview > Annotations (labels select objects, annotations do not); Argo CD docs: User Guide > Sync Phases and Waves (default wave 0)

claims.text: Argo CD applies the next wave only once the resources of the current wave are synced and healthy; it does not wait between objects of the same wave. A hook's wave is done when the hook ends (Succeeded continues, Failed fails the sync).
claims.source_hint: Argo CD docs: User Guide > Sync Phases and Waves (next wave = first wave with a resource out-of-sync or unhealthy)

claims.text: A hook is a resource annotated argocd.argoproj.io/hook; any kind (Pod, among others). A phase says when a hook runs, e.g. before, with or after the apply (not the full list). Non-hook resources are applied in the Sync phase, so a Sync hook shares their phase and its wave orders it.
claims.source_hint: Argo CD docs: User Guide > Resource Hooks (Usage, hook types: Sync 'at the same time as the apply of the manifests'); Sync Phases and Waves

claims.text: Argo CD creates hook resources during each sync rather than keeping them in place and comparing them with Git like other resources; hooks run on every sync of the whole Application, whether or not their manifest changed (selective sync not covered).
claims.source_hint: Argo CD docs: User Guide > Resource Hooks; examples/don-hang @ stage-3 outputs/stage-3/scripts/devops/gitops-order.txt (second sync with nothing changed: 'a new Pod migrate ran: Succeeded')

claims.text: The annotation argocd.argoproj.io/hook-delete-policy sets when Argo CD deletes a hook; BeforeHookCreation deletes the existing hook resource before the new one is created (the lesson does not say in which wave the deletion happens).
claims.source_hint: Argo CD docs: User Guide > Resource Hooks (Hook Deletion Policies)

claims.text: Two Pods cannot have the same name in one namespace (object names are unique per kind within a namespace), so a new migrate Pod cannot be created while the old one exists.
claims.source_hint: Kubernetes docs: Concepts > Overview > Object Names and IDs

claims.text: With restartPolicy: Never a container that exits non-zero is not restarted and the Pod ends Failed; a hook Pod that ends Failed fails the sync, later waves (the api, wave 2) are not applied and the live Deployment api is left unchanged. Not shown by the script; stated in words only.
claims.source_hint: Kubernetes docs: Pod Lifecycle (restartPolicy, Pod phase Failed); Argo CD docs: Resource Hooks / Sync Phases and Waves (failed hook fails the sync); migrate-hook.yaml:1-6 comment

Listed by name, api.yaml comes before db.yaml and migrate-hook.yaml.

claims.text: The db Deployment counts as healthy once its Pod passes its readiness probe (pg_isready over TCP); a Deployment is Healthy when its rollout is complete.
claims.source_hint: Argo CD docs: Operator Manual > Resource Health (Deployment); examples/don-hang @ stage-3 envs/staging/db.yaml readinessProbe

claims.text: The EF Core migration bundle applies only migrations not yet recorded in the database; with none pending it prints 'No migrations were applied. The database is already up to date.' and exits successfully.
claims.source_hint: EF Core docs: Applying Migrations > Bundles; examples/don-hang @ stage-3 outputs/stage-3/scripts/devops/gitops-order.txt (last lines)

With more than one api replica, one migration before the api is applied is safer than each replica migrating at startup; EF Core docs prefer a separate migration step when the rollout must be coordinated or the app must stay up. For one copy in local development it is acceptable.
claims.source_hint: EF Core docs: Applying Migrations > Apply migrations at runtime (EF Core 9+ database-wide lock; separate step still preferred for coordinated rollout / high availability)
